answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 32% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the farming party's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the timber reward in the whisper ledger costs the operator directly, and the walnut audit records each payout. A farm of 137 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
